handbookNote: Source: official 'Missouri Driver Guide -- A guide to understanding Missouri Motor Vehicle Laws and Licensing Requirements,' Revised August 2025, published by the Missouri Department of Revenue (DOR), Driver License Bureau. Retrieved directly from dor.mo.gov: dor.mo.gov/driver-license/ links to dor.mo.gov/driver-license/guide, which links directly to the PDF at https://dor.mo.gov/forms/Driver%20Guide.pdf. Downloaded via direct HTTP (curl); dor.mo.gov's public pages and /forms/ PDFs are not behind any bot-detection interstitial, so no browser session was needed. The PDF (102 pages, ~2.29MB) was confirmed a genuine text-based PDF (not a scanned image); full text was extracted natively via pdftotext -layout (not OCR) and archived to temp/handbooks/mo/driver.txt with a documented retrieval-method header, distinct from and not overwriting the existing mo notary handbook file in that same folder. Exam mechanics were confirmed directly from this guide itself, not guessed: p.1 states, 'To test your knowledge of traffic laws, you will need to take a written test of 25 multiple-choice questions... You must correctly answer 20 questions to pass the test.' That is confirmed as 25 items and an 80% (20/25) passing score for the Class F (standard operator) written knowledge test, restated identically in Chapter 2 'The Driver Examination' (p.18). The guide does NOT state a time limit anywhere for the written test (a targeted search of the full extracted text for 'minute,' 'timed,' and 'time limit' found no written-test timing statement -- the only 'minute' references are an unrelated two-minute parallel-parking window on the driving skills test and general safe-driving mentions). A follow-up check of the Missouri State Highway Patrol (MSHP) site, which administers the exam, did not surface a published time limit either, so the written test's time limit is reported honestly as unconfirmed/not found in official sources, rather than invented. Content-depth rationale: this August 2025 guide is substantial (102 pages, ~259KB of extracted text) with well-differentiated chapters on licensing/permits/GDL, the four-part driver examination, rules of the road (right-of-way, intersections, roundabouts, J-turns, school buses), sharing the road (motorcycles, large trucks, pedestrians, bicycles/mopeds/e-bikes, funeral processions, road rage), parking, highway driving (entrance/exit ramps, DDIs, highway hypnosis), pavement markings/signs/signals (including a full state-specific speed-limit table by roadway type), everyday and special-condition safe-driving tips (seat belts/child restraints, following/stopping distance, night/winter/wet-weather driving, skids, ABS, vehicle emergencies), alcohol/drugs and DWI law (BAC thresholds and penalty tables), the points system, vehicle titling/registration, mandatory insurance (with exact minimum coverage dollar figures), safety/emissions inspections and required equipment, and distracted driving/electronic communication device law. The guide itself states the Class F written test excludes Chapter 15 (Commercial Vehicles) -- 'You will not be tested on the information on commercial vehicles in Chapter 15' -- so that chapter was deliberately excluded from question content. This comfortably supported 281 distinct, grounded, non-repetitive multiple-choice questions across 16 topic buckets, all traceable to specific guide sections and page numbers cited in each question's source_note -- no invented facts, no generic 'common driving knowledge' not actually present in this source.
